features.name: Caesar and affine cipher with live cipher wheel
features.behaviour: User types plaintext, picks Caesar (shift k) or affine (a, b) and sees ciphertext update live on a rotating alphabet wheel; decrypt runs the inverse map
features.acceptance: E(x)=(x+3) mod 26 turns HELLO into KHOOR and decrypting returns HELLO; affine with a=5,b=8 turns AFFINE CIPHER into IHHWVC SWFRCP; an affine key with gcd(a,26)!=1 is rejected with a reason; D(E(m))=m for all 26 shifts and all 312 valid affine keys

features.name: Simple substitution cipher with permutation key editor
features.behaviour: User edits a 26-letter substitution key by swapping letters in an alphabet-mapping board; the key must stay a bijection; encrypt and decrypt use the map and its inverse
features.acceptance: A key with a repeated or missing letter is rejected and the duplicate is named; decrypt(encrypt(m)) equals m for a random valid permutation; case and non-letters are preserved

features.name: Letter-frequency analysis
features.behaviour: User pastes ciphertext and sees letter counts, relative frequencies as a histogram beside the English reference, and the index of coincidence
features.acceptance: For input AAB the counts are A=2, B=1 and the others 0; frequencies sum to 1 within 1e-9; non-letters are ignored; empty input returns a clear empty state, not NaN

features.name: Automated break by frequency analysis
features.behaviour: User runs the break on ciphertext; the app scores all 26 shifts (and all 312 affine keys) with a chi-squared test against English, ranks them and shows the winning key with plaintext, while the histogram visibly slides into alignment
features.acceptance: On the bundled sample Caesar ciphertext the top-ranked candidate is the true key and its plaintext equals the original; candidates are sorted by ascending chi-squared; ciphertext shorter than 20 letters returns a low-confidence warning

features.name: Math Lab: step-by-step modular arithmetic trace
features.behaviour: For any encryption or decryption the user can open a per-letter trace (x, key, computation, mod 26, result), the table of units mod 26 with inverses, and key-space counts for each cipher
features.acceptance: Trace rows reproduce the cipher output exactly for every letter; the inverse table lists the 12 units mod 26 with a*a^-1 = 1 mod 26; key-space counts shown are 26 (Caesar), 312 (affine), and 403291461126605635584000000 (substitution, 26!)

differentiators.name: Every output is a visible proof step
differentiators.why: The report is graded on the mathematics, so the app shows Z26 arithmetic, modular inverses via gcd and the group structure of shifts rather than just producing ciphertext
differentiators.demonstrated_by: Math Lab panel in the UI plus a unit test asserting trace rows equal cipher output

differentiators.name: Exhaustive self-verification panel
differentiators.why: Correctness is a hard limit; the app proves D(E(m))=m over every Caesar key and every valid affine key and checks that substitution keys are bijections
differentiators.demonstrated_by: Run-all-checks button in the UI and a property test script that prints pass counts (26 of 26, 312 of 312)

differentiators.name: Explainable break with chi-squared table
differentiators.why: A break that only shows the answer teaches nothing; showing the score of every candidate key and the sliding histogram explains why one key wins
differentiators.demonstrated_by: Ranked candidate table with chi-squared values and animated histogram alignment on the sample ciphertext

differentiators.name: Group explorer for Z26
differentiators.why: Shows the algebra behind the ciphers: (Z26,+) is a cyclic group, every unit generates it, and the units mod 26 form a group under multiplication, which is exactly why only 12 values of a work in the affine cipher
differentiators.demonstrated_by: Interactive orbit diagram and Cayley table; clicking an element shows its order and whether it is a generator; unit test asserts 12 units and that each unit has order dividing 12

differentiators.name: Algebraic key recovery from known plaintext
differentiators.why: A second attack that uses linear congruences instead of statistics: two known plaintext/ciphertext pairs give a(x1-x2) = y1-y2 (mod 26), solved with the modular inverse, and the app flags when gcd(x1-x2,26)>1 gives several solutions
differentiators.demonstrated_by: Known-plaintext panel that recovers (a,b) and lists all solutions when the congruence is not unique; test with the AFFINE CIPHER example

differentiators.name: Unicity distance and break-success curve
differentiators.why: Connects counting to cryptanalysis: key-space size (26, 312, 26!) determines how much ciphertext is needed before the key is unique, and the app measures how break accuracy rises with text length
differentiators.demonstrated_by: Chart of break success rate versus ciphertext length over random samples, plus the computed unicity distance per cipher; deterministic seeded run so results are reproducible
